title: Yehudah ben Dorta’i
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He lived in the time of Shemaya and Avtalyon. In [Pesachim 70b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.70b.5) it is related that he withdrew together with his son Dorta'i and settled in the south (far from Jerusalem), and said: "I am astonished at the two great ones of the generation, Shemaya and Avtalyon, who are great sages and expounders, yet did not tell Israel that the festival offering (chagigah) overrides the Sabbath"; and on account of this they withdrew. [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1627&lang=en) wrote: "And it appears that he was a Sadducee" — may his Master forgive him for this.

notes.text: The linked baraita records the departure and disagreement about the festival offering. Heilprin adds his conjecture that Yehudah ben Dorta’i was a Sadducee. “May his Master forgive him for this” is Hyman’s rebuke of Heilprin.
